Folks — below are three practical sizing paths and lead-time guidance. These are estimates based on similar EMR/healthcare customers with mixed short/long generation patterns. Numbers assume modern LLM (70B-ish), quantized execution, and our prefix caching enabled.

Option A — Conservatively small (cost-minimized, gradual ramp)
- Pool: 6 x A100-80GB equivalent
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~110 reqs/sec (avg payload 1.2k tokens total)
- P95 latency: ~380–420ms depending on burst
- Recommended commit: monthly reserved throughput + 20% burst credits
- Lead time: Dedicated reservation ~6 weeks; Private on-prem ~12 weeks (hardware ordering earliest).

Option B — Balanced / Recommended for POC -> Pilot
- Pool: 10 x A100-80GB equivalent
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~180 reqs/sec
- P95 latency: ~300–360ms
- Recommended commit: 3–6 month reserved capacity with planned scale at pilot completion
- Lead time: Dedicated ~6–8 weeks; Private ~12–14 weeks including integration testing.

Option C — Aggressive / low-latency target
- Pool: 18 x A100-80GB equivalent (or mixed with some H100s for burst-critical models)
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~320 reqs/sec
- P95 latency: ~220–300ms
- Recommended commit: 6–12 month reserved pool to secure capacity and pricing
- Lead time: Dedicated ~8 weeks; Private 14–16 weeks (longer if on-prem procurement windows are constrained).

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling & burst: we recommend a small burst buffer (10–30% depending on SLA) and routing fallback to hosted variants in other regions during provisioning spikes.
- KV/prefix cache: if you can provide sample prefix hit rates, we can tune pooling to reduce effective GPU needs.
- Hardware substitution: if H100/HDR options are available, latency improves but so do unit costs; we can provide mixed-pool pricing.

I've attached a procurement checklist and rough BOM assumptions in the shared drive doc. Happy to refine after we get average token lengths and concurrency percentiles from Orion.

— Karthik
